sql.demo:
SELECT c.name, count(*) AS orders
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.created_at > '2025-12-01'
GROUP BY c.name
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 10
sql.filter:
SELECT name, city
FROM customers
WHERE city = 'Pune'
ORDER BY name
sql.count:
SELECT count(*)
FROM orders
WHERE amount > 5
sql.cte:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT customer_id, sum(amount) AS total
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.name, b.total
FROM big b
JOIN customers c ON c.id = b.customer_id
WHERE b.total > 100
ORDER BY b.total DESC
sql.union:
SELECT id, name FROM customers
WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE amount > 5)
UNION ALL
SELECT id, name FROM customers
WHERE city = 'Pune'

demo.sql:
select c.name, count(*) n
from orders o
join customers c on c.id = o.customer_id
where o.status = 'paid'
group by c.name
having count(*) >= 2
order by n desc
limit 3

                        -> Filter: ((o.`status` = 'paid') and (o.customer_id is not null))  (cost=0.65 rows=1)
                            -> Table scan on o  (cost=0.65 rows=4)
                        -> Single-row index lookup on c using PRIMARY (id = o.customer_id)  (cost=0.35 rows=1)

select c.name, count(*) n
from orders o
join customers c on c.id = o.customer_id
where o.status = 'paid'
group by c.name
having count(*) >= 2
order by n desc
limit 3
